before: But if these powers belong to the soul itself, and it receives its better additions superabundantly, then surely the soul grows together with the body. Just as the body gradually develops its powers, so too the soul advances in mind. And those who never step toward what is better but remain foolish clearly have incomplete souls because some part has been damaged, just like those who have fallen ill with the disease of madness. Certainly the body of the first-formed human also lay dead after it was shaped—breathless, motionless, yet arranged to the highest degree in its limbs and joints, and fittingly adorned in form and beauty, since it was created by the Creator God himself as a first-model statue and impressed as the finest copy from the most divine image. But it was without sensation, without speech, and without breath. Then, when God breathed into its face in the manner of a craftsman, it immediately received movement. From that moment it walks and breathes and speaks; it rules, reasons, acts, administers. In this way, sleep is a condition common to body and soul.
